statement: A top-10 economy legally authorises fully automated decisions (no human sign-off) in a new benefits, tax or immigration domain (official gazette; OECD.AI; by 2028-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not met in 2024; the legal trend ran mostly toward NO. Bloc A's federal budget office required minimum practices including human review/appeal for rights-impacting AI (explicitly covering benefits and immigration). The supranational AI regulation covering three top-10 economies was published and entered into force, classifying benefits and migration AI as high-risk with mandatory human oversight. The one YES-leaning item: a top-10 economy reintroduced a data bill (after an earlier version lapsed) that would relax its general ban on solely automated significant decisions - pending at year-end and not domain-specific.

items.summary: Bloc A's federal budget office set binding minimum practices for 'rights-impacting' government AI by Dec 2024: impact assessments, human oversight, notice, and human consideration/remedy or opt-out. Benefits eligibility and immigration decisions were presumed rights-impacting.
items.detail: OMB Memorandum M-24-10 'Advancing Governance, Innovation, and Risk Management for Agency Use of AI', 2024-03-28 (Bloc A). Executive guidance, not statute.

items.summary: A supranational AI regulation covering three top-10 economies was published in the official journal (in force 1 Aug 2024). It lists AI for public-benefit eligibility and for migration, asylum and border control as high-risk, requiring human oversight once high-risk obligations apply (Aug 2026).
items.detail: Regulation (Bloc C) 2024/1689 (Bloc C AI Act), OJ L 2024-07-12; Annex III points 5(a) and 7; Art. 14 human oversight. Bloc D, Bloc E, Bloc F are top-10 economies.

items.summary: A top-10 economy's bill that would have relaxed its ban on solely automated significant decisions lapsed when parliament was dissolved before an election.
items.detail: Bloc G Data Protection and Digital Information Bill (would have replaced Bloc G GDPR Art. 22) fell at the dissolution of Parliament announced 2024-05-22 / prorogued 2024-05-24. Not re-extracted this run.

items.summary: The same top-10 economy's new government introduced a successor data bill again allowing solely automated significant decisions on most lawful bases, with safeguards (information, human intervention on request, contestation). Pending at end-2024; general, not specific to benefits, tax or immigration.
items.detail: Bloc G Data (Use and Access) Bill, introduced in the House of Lords 2024-10-23 (clause on new Bloc G GDPR Arts 22A-22D). Enacted 2025-06-19 (after phase; not used for as-of status).

items.summary: No 2024 statute found in Bloc A, Bloc B or other top-10 economies newly authorising fully automated decisions in benefits, tax or immigration. Bloc B and several other top-10 gazettes not systematically searched.
items.detail: Pre-existing bases (Bloc D § 155(4) AO tax, § 31a SGB X social) predate 2024. Bloc B, Bloc N, Bloc O, Bloc P, Bloc Q not systematically checked.
